title: Global counit transposition determines the finite reduction of a tower pair
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms. Put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\ge1$. For a scheme $T$ use the ordinary derived category $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$ of strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Write $\mathcal C_T$ for its full subcategory whose levels have bounded intrinsically constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, in common intervals independent of $n$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. No normalization is required. At level $n$ write $\mathcal C_{T,n}=D^b_{ctf}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ in the ordinary constant-ring module derived category. For each separated finite-type map $h$ choose a coefficient-independent compactification and write $F_h=Rh_{!,\bullet}$ and $F_{h,n}=Rh_{!,A_n}$ [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], using the same chosen coefficient-independent compactification in $F_f$, all $F_{f,n}$, and the finite coefficient comparisons. Let $G\in\mathcal C_X$, $K\in\mathcal C_Y$, and $\epsilon:F_fG\to K$ be an actual derived tower morphism. Assume that for every $n$ its evaluation $(G_n,\epsilon_n)$ is a representing pair for $M\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(F_{f,n}M,K_n)$ on all of $\mathcal C_{X,n}$. Fix the unique counit-preserving identifications $\iota_n:G_n\xrightarrow{\sim}f^!_{A_n}K_n$ with the finite adjoints of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional].

For $1\le m\le n$, write $(C_n)_{A_m}=C_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$ and let $r_G:(G_n)_{A_m}\to G_m$ and $r_K:(K_n)_{A_m}\to K_m$ be the canonical reductions [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. The canonical isomorphism
$$b_f(G_n):(F_{f,n}G_n)_{A_m}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f,m}((G_n)_{A_m})$$
is the proper-counit transpose followed by the open tensor comparison specified in [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. The actual tower counit satisfies the global derived equality
$$\epsilon_mF_{f,m}(r_G)=r_K(\epsilon_n)_{A_m}b_f(G_n)^{-1}.$$
Both sides have source $F_{f,m}((G_n)_{A_m})$ and target $K_m$.

The finite scalar extension $(G_n)_{A_m}$ remains ctf [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], and under $\iota_n,\iota_m$ the reduction is
$$r_G=f^!_{A_m}(r_K)\circ c_{n,m}(K_n),$$
where $c_{n,m}(K_n):(f^!_{A_n}K_n)_{A_m}\xrightarrow{\sim}f^!_{A_m}((K_n)_{A_m})$ is the specified coefficient comparison [det-sp-reduction-exceptional]. Its defining counit transpose and that of $r_G$ both equal the displayed global map. These formulas hold for arbitrary, possibly ramified $E$, without normalization of either tower or flatness or finite projective dimension of $A_m$ over $A_n$. They are identities for $m=n$ and respect triple reductions $n\ge m\ge r\ge1$ under derived tensor associativity. The quotient maps are unital, the rings $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{en}$ and $A_m=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{em}$ are finite, and both are killed by the common annihilator $\ell^n$.

proof.text: Use the supplied Base.finite and Base.ideals for finiteness and the ramification equality. For m≤n, l^(n+1) belongs to (l)^(n+1) contained in (l)^(m+1), so its quotient class is zero and it annihilates A_m. The supplied hS already proves scalar extension remains ctf. Apply det-sp-reduction-direct-image to G_n, using its finite cohomological support and the same common annihilator, to obtain the isomorphism bi with the specified hom.

The coordinate-conversion step [lem-sp-intrinsic-shriek-transition] gives T(v_n) b F_m(r_G)=r_FG v_m in the actual intrinsic coordinates of this item. Naturality of the reduction transformation at epsilon and cancellation of the evaluation isomorphisms give F_m(r_G) epsilon_m = bi.inv T(epsilon_n) r_K.

The inverse Hom equivalence applied to comparison immediately gives its defining finite counit equation. Compose with H_m(r_K) and use counit naturality to obtain the displayed exceptional counit equation. For invertibility, det-sp-reduction-exceptional supplies some finite adjoints and an invertible comparison with this equation. The unique counit-preserving right-adjoint isomorphisms conjugate it to the supplied adjoints H_n,H_m; injectivity of the inverse Hom equivalence proves the conjugacy. Hence comparison is invertible for these supplied adjoints as well.

Apply the injective inverse Hom equivalence of adj_m to the transported actual reduction and the exceptional reduction word. Counit preservation at m and n, Step 2, and inverse naturality of the specified b show their transposes coincide; cancel iota_n.inv iota_n. The ctf test object is scalar extension of H_n(K_n), justified directly by the supplied hS.

Conjugate the recorded reduction_identity and reduction_comp fields by the scalar coordinates to prove ReductionCoherent on every derived tower, hence on G,K,FG. Conjugate the identities on G through iota: functoriality cancels the intermediate iota_m and its inverse, and naturality of scalarUnit/scalarAssoc moves the outer iota_n inverse. Substitute Step 4 to obtain the exceptional identity and triple equations.
